title: The Xerox Alto and the Desktop Metaphor (1973)
explainer: Long before 'folder' and 'file' were screen icons, they were literal words researchers at Xerox PARC chose when they built the Alto, one of the first computers to represent a hierarchical filesystem visually instead of only through typed commands. The mental model you're building in this lesson - files living inside directories inside directories - is the same tree structure that GUI desktops and the command line simply describe in two different vocabularies, which is why 'folder' and 'directory' refer to the exact same thing.
